name: Semaglutide
summary: Semaglutide is an established prescription GLP-1 medicine with formulation-specific roles in type 2 diabetes, weight management, cardiovascular risk reduction, kidney protection and selected liver disease. Benefits and eligibility depend on the actual approved product, rather than the ingredient name alone.
description: Semaglutide appears in Ozempic, Rybelsus and Wegovy, but these products have different evidence, indications and delivery systems. Current Wegovy labeling includes injectable and oral formulations for adult weight management and cardiovascular risk reduction in eligible patients; the injection also has pediatric obesity and selected MASH indications. Ozempic has diabetes, cardiovascular and kidney-outcome indications in defined adult populations. Oral absorption depends on the formulation, so tablet and injectable amounts are not interchangeable. This is a medicine for diagnosed conditions with ongoing follow-up, not evidence that semaglutide benefits every person seeking metabolic optimization.
mechanism: Semaglutide activates the glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor. It increases insulin secretion and lowers glucagon when glucose is elevated, influences appetite and food intake, and delays gastric emptying. Structural changes and albumin binding prolong exposure compared with the short-lived natural hormone. Appetite reduction contributes substantially to weight loss, while clinical trials establish specific cardiovascular and kidney benefits that cannot be inferred from weight change alone.
keyTakeaway: Semaglutide has strong clinical evidence, but its benefits must be matched to the formulation and patient population studied. The current label, medical history and treatment goals determine suitability.

sections.title: Approved uses and product differences
sections.body: Wegovy injection includes obesity treatment from age 12 and, in adults, noncirrhotic MASH with F2–F3 fibrosis under accelerated approval. Oral Wegovy has adult weight and cardiovascular indications. Ozempic’s current label includes adults with type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease.

sections.title: What the major trials show
sections.body: STEP 1 established substantial weight reduction in adults without diabetes. SELECT demonstrated fewer major cardiovascular events in adults with established cardiovascular disease and overweight or obesity. These were different populations and endpoints; one result should not be substituted for another.

sections.title: Adverse effects and important exclusions
sections.body: Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea and constipation are common. Labels address pancreatitis, gallbladder disease, dehydration-related kidney injury, severe gastrointestinal reactions and aspiration during anesthesia. Semaglutide is contraindicated with a personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma or MEN2; the thyroid warning originates in rodent findings.

sections.title: What follow-up considers
sections.body: Diabetes treatment may require attention to hypoglycemia when insulin or insulin secretagogues are also used. Retinopathy history, kidney function during dehydration, gastrointestinal tolerance and pregnancy plans affect clinical management. Product switching requires a prescribing plan because exposure and indications differ.

sections.title: What accelerated MASH approval means
sections.body: The MASH indication was supported by improvement in liver inflammation and fibrosis. Continued approval may depend on confirmation of clinical benefit. This does not establish reversal of cirrhosis or suitability for every cause of abnormal liver tests.

sections.title: Common questions
sections.body:
Are Ozempic and Wegovy interchangeable? They contain the same active ingredient, but their approved indications, formulations and instructions differ. Product-specific information remains necessary.

Does a weight-management approval also establish every liver benefit? No. Wegovy's MASH indication concerns a defined noncirrhotic population and uses an accelerated approval pathway; it is not an approval for every fatty-liver condition.

name: Tirzepatide
molecularClass: Dual GIP and GLP-1 receptor agonist peptide
summary: Tirzepatide activates two incretin receptors and is an approved medicine for type 2 diabetes and, in a separate product, chronic weight management and obesity-associated obstructive sleep apnea. Its substantial average effects in trials coexist with gastrointestinal risks and product-specific eligibility requirements.
description: Mounjaro and Zepbound contain tirzepatide but serve different approved indications. Mounjaro is used for type 2 diabetes, while Zepbound supports long-term weight reduction in eligible adults and treats moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnea in adults with obesity. Sleep-apnea approval does not replace an individualized assessment of airway treatment or positive-airway-pressure needs. Trial averages describe groups receiving a manufactured, regulated product with clinical follow-up. They do not predict an individual response or validate mixed research products sold under the same ingredient name.
mechanism: Tirzepatide activates glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide and GLP-1 receptors. These pathways influence glucose-dependent insulin secretion, glucagon regulation and food intake. Its fatty-acid side chain supports albumin binding and a prolonged action suitable for weekly administration. Reduced appetite and caloric intake contribute to weight loss; delayed gastric emptying also influences tolerability and absorption of some oral medicines.
keyTakeaway: Tirzepatide has strong evidence for defined metabolic conditions. The correct product, indication and monitoring matter, particularly when diabetes medicines, oral contraception, severe gastrointestinal disease or sleep-apnea treatment are involved.

sections.title: How the approved products differ
sections.body: Zepbound’s current label covers adults with obesity or qualifying overweight, plus moderate-to-severe OSA in adults with obesity. Mounjaro is a diabetes product. Neither indication establishes tirzepatide as a treatment for type 1 diabetes or every cause of fatigue or weight gain.

sections.title: Weight and sleep-apnea evidence
sections.body: SURMOUNT-1 found considerably greater weight reduction with tirzepatide than placebo in adults with obesity without diabetes. The FDA’s sleep-apnea approval relied on separate trials measuring apnea-hypopnea events. Weight-loss findings and airway outcomes answer related but different clinical questions.

sections.title: Major precautions
sections.body: The label warns about severe gastrointestinal reactions, pancreatitis, gallbladder disease, dehydration-related kidney injury and serious allergy. Hypoglycemia risk rises with insulin or insulin secretagogues. Personal or family medullary thyroid cancer and MEN2 are contraindications; human relevance of the rodent thyroid findings remains uncertain.

sections.title: Medicines and procedures
sections.body: Delayed gastric emptying can affect oral medicines. Label-specific precautions apply to oral hormonal contraception during initiation and escalation. Anesthesia teams need to know about use because pulmonary aspiration has been reported with GLP-1 medicines during general anesthesia or deep sedation.

sections.title: Interpreting a response
sections.body: Weight change is only one outcome. Glycemic control, treatment tolerance, nutrition and sleep-apnea symptoms may all influence follow-up. Combining tirzepatide products or adding another GLP-1 receptor agonist is not recommended in Zepbound labeling.

sections.title: Common questions
sections.body:
Is Zepbound the same treatment as Mounjaro? Both contain tirzepatide, but the brands have different approved clinical uses and product labeling.

Does improvement in weight automatically establish sleep-apnea treatment? The sleep-apnea indication rests on specific studies and applies to adults with obesity and moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnea. Other sleep disorders or populations require separate evidence.

name: Dasiglucagon
summary: Dasiglucagon is a ready-to-use glucagon analog for severe hypoglycemia in people with diabetes aged six years and older. It is an emergency rescue medicine that raises glucose through the liver, with effectiveness limited when hepatic glycogen stores are depleted.
description: Marketed as Zegalogue, dasiglucagon provides a stable liquid glucagon formulation for situations in which a person cannot safely manage severe low glucose themselves. Its purpose is rapid rescue, not routine adjustment of daily diabetes control. Severe hypoglycemia can involve confusion, seizures or unconsciousness, so a rescue plan includes caregiver recognition and emergency assistance. The product differs from older glucagon kits that require preparation, and from nasal glucagon. Those differences concern delivery and handling as well as the active molecule; products must be used according to their own instructions.
mechanism: Dasiglucagon binds the glucagon receptor in liver cells and stimulates glycogen breakdown, releasing glucose into the circulation. It has amino-acid substitutions that improve stability in an aqueous formulation while retaining glucagon activity. A response requires sufficient stored liver glycogen. Prolonged fasting, starvation, adrenal insufficiency or chronic hypoglycemia can reduce that reserve and make glucagon rescue less effective.
keyTakeaway: Dasiglucagon is an evidence-based emergency treatment for severe low glucose. Ready-to-use packaging simplifies rescue, but caregivers still need product training and a clear emergency plan because response is not guaranteed.

sections.title: When it is used
sections.body: The FDA indication is severe hypoglycemia in adults and children aged six or older with diabetes. It is not an obesity medicine or a substitute for preventing recurrent low-glucose episodes through review of the diabetes regimen.

sections.title: What the pivotal trial measured
sections.body: A randomized phase 3 trial used controlled insulin-induced hypoglycemia and measured time to plasma-glucose recovery. Dasiglucagon produced faster recovery than placebo, supporting emergency rescue efficacy. The controlled study environment does not remove the need for emergency help in actual severe events.

sections.title: Contraindications and adverse effects
sections.body: Nausea, vomiting, headache and injection-site discomfort occur. Pheochromocytoma is a contraindication because glucagon activity can provoke marked blood-pressure increases; insulinoma is also a contraindication because an initial glucose rise can trigger excessive insulin release. Serious allergic reactions are possible.

sections.title: Why rescue may fail
sections.body: Glucagon cannot create a useful glucose response without adequate hepatic glycogen. Persistent or recurrent hypoglycemia requires further medical assessment. The cause of the episode, ongoing insulin action and nutritional status matter even when the initial glucose response is satisfactory.

sections.title: A rescue medicine needs a rescue plan
sections.body: Caregivers need to know where the device is kept and how its specific mechanism works. Product availability and an unexpired device do not ensure that an unfamiliar bystander can use it correctly during an emergency.

name: Ga-68 dotatate
summary: Gallium-68 dotatate is a diagnostic radiopharmaceutical used in PET imaging of somatostatin receptor-positive neuroendocrine tumors. The peptide guides a radioactive tracer to receptor-expressing tissue; imaging identifies its distribution rather than treating the tumor.
description: Netspot is a preparation kit used to produce gallium-68 dotatate for specialist nuclear-medicine imaging. Many well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumors express somatostatin receptors, allowing this tracer to help locate disease and characterize receptor expression. Findings can contribute to staging and treatment planning, including assessment for receptor-targeted radionuclide therapy. The result is interpreted with clinical information and other imaging. A bright focus is not automatically malignant, and a negative scan does not exclude every neuroendocrine tumor, especially when receptor expression is low or heterogeneous.
mechanism: Dotatate binds somatostatin receptors, particularly subtype 2. Gallium-68 attached through a chelator emits positrons, which generate the signal detected by PET. Uptake depends on receptor expression and normal tracer handling. Physiologic activity in organs and uptake in nonmalignant conditions can complicate interpretation. Unlike lutetium-177 dotatate, the gallium-labeled preparation is optimized for imaging rather than therapeutic radiation delivery.
keyTakeaway: Ga-68 dotatate is an established tumor-imaging tool, not a wellness peptide or cancer treatment by itself. Its usefulness depends on receptor biology, expert interpretation and the clinical question being investigated.

sections.title: Approved imaging role
sections.body: The U.S. indication is PET localization of somatostatin receptor-positive neuroendocrine tumors in adults and children. The study is organized by a nuclear-medicine service with licensed radiopharmaceutical preparation and radiation-safety procedures.

sections.title: Why receptor imaging is useful
sections.body: A prospective study evaluated detection of gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumors and unknown primary sites with gallium-68 dotatate. It demonstrated clinically useful lesion detection compared with conventional approaches, but detection performance depends on tumor type and the reference standard used.

sections.title: What uptake does and does not mean
sections.body: Normal tissues, inflammatory processes and some non-neuroendocrine tumors may take up tracer. Tumors with little somatostatin receptor expression can be missed. The scan therefore supports a diagnostic assessment; it does not independently establish histology or replace all other tests.

sections.title: Radiation and patient considerations
sections.body: Exposure adds to cumulative medical radiation. Hypersensitivity reactions are possible. Pregnancy, breastfeeding, renal clearance and other somatostatin-directed medicines require attention to the product label and nuclear-medicine protocol because they affect safety or image interpretation.

sections.title: Relationship to Lu-177 dotatate
sections.body: Both agents use receptor-targeted peptide delivery, but the isotope changes the purpose. Ga-68 primarily provides a PET signal; Lu-177 delivers therapeutic beta radiation. A diagnostic scan and a radionuclide treatment are separate procedures with different risk profiles.

name: Glucagon
molecularClass: Pancreatic peptide hormone and pharmaceutical rescue hormone
summary: Glucagon is a glucose-raising peptide hormone used in approved rescue products for severe hypoglycemia and in some diagnostic procedures. Injectable and nasal products differ in preparation, age eligibility and administration; all depend substantially on available liver glycogen.
description: The body releases glucagon from pancreatic alpha cells to help maintain blood glucose during fasting. Pharmaceutical glucagon turns that physiology into an emergency treatment for severe low glucose, especially when a person cannot safely swallow. Approved products include traditional injection kits and ready-to-use injectable or nasal formulations. Some injectable labeling also covers temporary inhibition of gastrointestinal movement during diagnostic examinations. These are distinct indications: a diagnostic product or device should not be assumed equivalent to a particular home rescue product merely because it contains glucagon.
mechanism: Glucagon activates a G-protein-coupled receptor that increases intracellular cyclic AMP, especially in the liver. This promotes glycogen breakdown and glucose release. Its gastrointestinal smooth-muscle effects support selected diagnostic uses. A rescue response can be inadequate after prolonged fasting or in other conditions with depleted liver glycogen, so the hormone is not a universal solution for every cause of low glucose.
keyTakeaway: Glucagon is established emergency care for severe hypoglycemia, with several delivery options. Choosing and learning the actual rescue product matters as much as knowing the hormone’s name.

sections.title: Rescue and diagnostic indications
sections.body: Baqsimi is a nasal glucagon rescue product, while GlucaGen and other injectable products have their own indications and age instructions. Gastrointestinal diagnostic use belongs to particular injectable labels and should not be generalized to every glucagon formulation.

sections.title: Evidence for nasal delivery
sections.body: A randomized crossover study in adults with type 1 diabetes compared nasal and intramuscular glucagon during induced hypoglycemia. Both achieved the study’s recovery criteria in nearly all administrations. This supports nasal delivery without requiring the person to inhale deliberately.

sections.title: Known adverse effects
sections.body: Nausea and vomiting are common across rescue formulations; nasal products can cause nasal or eye irritation. Serious allergy can occur. Pheochromocytoma and insulinoma are important contraindications because glucagon can provoke dangerous hormonal responses in these conditions.

sections.title: The glycogen limitation
sections.body: Prolonged fasting, starvation, adrenal insufficiency and chronic hypoglycemia may leave inadequate hepatic glycogen for a useful response. A severe episode remains an emergency even if a rescue product has been given, and recurrent episodes require investigation of the underlying cause.

sections.title: Why product training matters
sections.body: An injectable kit requiring preparation, a ready-to-use device and a nasal dispenser involve different actions under stress. A household rescue plan should correspond to the prescribed product and the people likely to assist, rather than relying on generic instructions for glucagon.

name: Lanreotide
summary: Lanreotide is an approved somatostatin analog for acromegaly, selected gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumors and carcinoid syndrome. It suppresses hormone secretion and can delay tumor progression in a defined tumor population, while requiring attention to gallbladder, glucose and digestive effects.
description: Somatuline Depot provides sustained lanreotide exposure through a deep subcutaneous formulation. In acromegaly, the aim is control of excessive growth-hormone activity when surgery or radiotherapy is inadequate or unsuitable. In unresectable, well- or moderately differentiated gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumors, its role includes improving progression-free survival. It also reduces reliance on short-acting rescue treatment for carcinoid syndrome. Control of flushing or diarrhea, normalization of hormone levels and slowing tumor progression are different outcomes, and the appropriate endpoint depends on the disease being treated.
mechanism: Lanreotide mimics somatostatin, an inhibitory hormone with receptors on endocrine and neuroendocrine cells. Receptor activation suppresses growth hormone and several gastrointestinal or pancreatic secretions. In responsive tumors, receptor signaling can also reduce proliferative activity. Suppressing insulin, glucagon and digestive secretions explains why treatment can change blood glucose and cause fat malabsorption alongside its intended endocrine effects.
keyTakeaway: Lanreotide is a specialist endocrine and oncology medicine with established uses. Symptom improvement does not by itself establish tumor shrinkage, so hormone tests, imaging and treatment tolerance remain separate parts of follow-up.

sections.title: Which tumors are covered
sections.body: The tumor indication concerns adults with unresectable, well- or moderately differentiated, locally advanced or metastatic gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumors. It does not cover all cancers or every tumor with a neuroendocrine label.

sections.title: Tumor-control evidence
sections.body: CLARINET studied lanreotide in advanced enteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumors and demonstrated longer progression-free survival than placebo. The principal finding was delayed progression in the enrolled population; this should not be described as proof that every treated tumor shrinks or is cured.

sections.title: Adverse effects and precautions
sections.body: Gallstones and related complications, abdominal symptoms, injection-site reactions and glucose disturbances are recognized. Bradycardia and thyroid-function changes can occur. New greasy stools, bloating or unintended weight loss may suggest pancreatic exocrine insufficiency rather than deterioration of the original disease.

sections.title: How response is assessed
sections.body: Acromegaly follow-up considers GH and IGF-1, while tumor care also uses imaging and clinical assessment. Diabetes and heart-rate-lowering medicines can complicate management. The label recommends attention to glucose, gallbladder and relevant thyroid abnormalities.

sections.title: How it differs from a tracer
sections.body: Lanreotide delivers a pharmacologic somatostatin signal. Radiolabeled dotatate compounds instead attach an imaging or therapeutic isotope to a receptor-targeting peptide. Sharing a receptor family does not make these products interchangeable.

name: Linaclotide
summary: Linaclotide is an oral, locally acting peptide for constipation disorders. Current U.S. labeling covers adult chronic idiopathic constipation, IBS with constipation from age seven and pediatric functional constipation from age two, with a boxed dehydration warning for younger children.
description: Linzess acts mainly within the intestinal lumen rather than requiring substantial systemic absorption. The intended outcomes are easier and more frequent bowel movements and, in IBS-C, improvement in associated abdominal symptoms. Diagnosis matters because constipation can result from obstruction, medicines, pelvic-floor problems or other diseases that a secretory agent does not correct. The October 2026 label contains broader pediatric indications than older summaries. Age thresholds differ by diagnosis, so an age-appropriate approval for functional constipation should not be mistaken for approval of every constipation-related condition in that child.
mechanism: Linaclotide and its active metabolite bind guanylate cyclase-C on intestinal epithelial cells. Increased intracellular cyclic GMP stimulates chloride and bicarbonate secretion through CFTR, drawing fluid into the lumen and accelerating transit. Extracellular cyclic GMP has reduced activity of pain-sensing nerves in animal experiments. That mechanistic observation helps explain development but should be distinguished from clinical symptom outcomes in people.
keyTakeaway: Linaclotide is a regulated treatment for specific constipation disorders, with age limits that depend on diagnosis. Local action does not eliminate risk: severe diarrhea and dehydration remain central safety concerns.

sections.title: Current approved populations
sections.body: U.S. labeling includes IBS-C in adults and children seven or older, chronic idiopathic constipation in adults, and functional constipation in children two or older. These indication-specific ages supersede older descriptions that restricted all pediatric use to age six or above.

sections.title: What trials measure
sections.body: Randomized IBS-C studies assessed both abdominal pain and complete spontaneous bowel movements. This distinction matters: more frequent stool passage and less abdominal pain are related but separate outcomes. Pediatric approvals rely on age- and indication-specific development, not simply extrapolation from adult doses.

sections.title: Diarrhea and dehydration
sections.body: Diarrhea is the major adverse effect and can be severe. Abdominal pain, gas and distension also occur. The boxed warning addresses serious dehydration in children younger than two, for whom the medicine is contraindicated.

sections.title: When the diagnosis changes the decision
sections.body: Known or suspected mechanical gastrointestinal obstruction is a contraindication. A secretory bowel medicine should not be treated as a way to push through an unexplained obstructive process. Persistent or changing symptoms can require reassessment of the original diagnosis.

sections.title: Does local action mean no systemic concerns?
sections.body: Minimal absorption limits direct systemic exposure, but excessive intestinal fluid loss can still have whole-body consequences. The relevant safety question is therefore both where the peptide acts and what the resulting diarrhea or dehydration does to the patient.

name: Liraglutide
molecularClass: Acylated human GLP-1 receptor agonist peptide
summary: Liraglutide is an approved daily GLP-1 medicine used in different products for type 2 diabetes and chronic weight management. Its cardiovascular evidence applies to defined diabetes populations, and the diabetes and weight-management products have different eligibility and prescribing requirements.
description: Victoza and Saxenda contain the same active peptide but are not identical treatment plans. Victoza is a diabetes medicine with cardiovascular-risk reduction for certain adults with type 2 diabetes; Saxenda is a weight-management product for eligible adults and adolescents. Current Saxenda labeling includes patients aged twelve and older with obesity who weigh more than sixty kilograms. A brand’s approved condition, age group and formulation determine the relevant evidence. Weight loss can occur during diabetes treatment, but that observation alone does not erase distinctions between the products or justify combining GLP-1 medicines.
mechanism: Liraglutide resembles endogenous GLP-1 and activates its receptor. This promotes glucose-dependent insulin release, reduces inappropriate glucagon secretion and affects appetite and gastric emptying. Acylation increases protein binding and, with resistance to enzymatic breakdown, extends its action beyond that of native GLP-1. The resulting pharmacokinetics support daily administration, unlike several later weekly GLP-1 analogs.
keyTakeaway: Liraglutide has established metabolic benefits when matched to the correct product and indication. Gastrointestinal tolerance, diabetes co-treatment, relevant endocrine history and long-term response guide its clinical use.

sections.title: Weight management versus diabetes care
sections.body: Saxenda labeling covers obesity and qualifying adult overweight alongside diet and physical activity. Victoza’s diabetes indication and cardiovascular indication are separate. Saxenda’s safety and effectiveness in pediatric patients with type 2 diabetes have not been established.

sections.title: Cardiovascular evidence
sections.body: LEADER enrolled adults with type 2 diabetes and high cardiovascular risk and found fewer major cardiovascular events with liraglutide than placebo. This supports the specified diabetes indication; it is not direct evidence of the same outcome in every younger person using liraglutide solely for weight management.

sections.title: Major adverse effects and exclusions
sections.body: Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea and constipation are common. Label warnings include pancreatitis, gallbladder disease, dehydration-related kidney injury and severe gastrointestinal reactions. A personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma or MEN2 is a contraindication because of the thyroid C-cell tumor concern.

sections.title: Clinical issues beyond body weight
sections.body: Heart rate, glucose when relevant, gastrointestinal tolerance and hydration can influence follow-up. Insulin or insulin secretagogues increase hypoglycemia concerns. Planned anesthesia, pregnancy and significant gastroparesis require attention to current product information and clinical assessment.

sections.title: Can the products be combined?
sections.body: Saxenda labeling does not recommend coadministration with other liraglutide products or another GLP-1 receptor agonist. Switching between daily and weekly agents requires a prescribing decision rather than treating their nominal amounts as equivalent.

name: Lutetium Lu-177 dotatate
summary: Lutetium Lu-177 dotatate is an approved peptide receptor radionuclide therapy for selected somatostatin receptor-positive neuroendocrine tumors. It delivers therapeutic radiation through receptor targeting and requires specialist oncology, nuclear-medicine and radiation-safety care, including blood, kidney and liver monitoring.
description: Lutathera treats gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumors in adults and children aged twelve and older when the tumors express somatostatin receptors. Patient selection depends on tumor biology, disease distribution, prior treatment and organ reserve. This is a radiopharmaceutical cancer treatment rather than a conventional hormone injection. Receptor imaging helps establish whether the target is present, while laboratory monitoring evaluates whether the patient can safely tolerate treatment. Its benefits concern tumor control in defined populations; the presence of a peptide component does not make it a general regenerative or longevity therapy.
mechanism: The dotatate component binds somatostatin receptors, with greatest affinity for SSTR2, and is internalized by receptor-expressing cells. Lutetium-177 emits beta radiation that damages the targeted cell and nearby cells. The same targeting principle can be paired with a diagnostic isotope, but therapeutic radiation produces different exposure and toxicity. Normal receptor-expressing tissues and renal handling also contribute to treatment considerations.
keyTakeaway: Lu-177 dotatate is established targeted radiotherapy for eligible neuroendocrine tumors. Demonstrating receptor expression is only one part of selection; organ function, marrow reserve and radiation precautions remain essential.

sections.title: Approved disease scope
sections.body: The U.S. indication includes somatostatin receptor-positive gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumors of the foregut, midgut and hindgut. Eligibility is not established by a tumor name alone; receptor expression and clinical assessment guide selection.

sections.title: Pivotal treatment evidence
sections.body: NETTER-1 compared Lu-177 dotatate plus long-acting octreotide with high-dose octreotide in progressive midgut neuroendocrine tumors. It showed substantially improved progression-free survival. The controlled evidence supports tumor control and should not be presented as universal cure or guaranteed symptom relief.

sections.title: Major treatment risks
sections.body: Bone-marrow suppression, kidney toxicity and liver toxicity require monitoring. Delayed myelodysplastic syndrome and leukemia are recognized risks. Hypersensitivity and neuroendocrine hormonal crises can occur, and radiation can harm a fetus or affect fertility.

sections.title: Why treatment requires specialist infrastructure
sections.body: Amino-acid support, laboratory follow-up and radiation-protection procedures are part of the labeled treatment framework. Medical personnel and household contacts can be exposed to radiation from the patient or excreta, so institution-specific release and home-safety instructions matter.

sections.title: A positive scan is not a complete treatment decision
sections.body: Receptor-targeted imaging indicates where a radiolabeled peptide accumulates. It does not independently establish adequate marrow, kidney or liver reserve or determine the best place of radionuclide treatment among other oncology options.

name: Octreotide
summary: Octreotide suppresses several endocrine and gastrointestinal secretions and is an established treatment for acromegaly and hormone-driven symptoms of selected neuroendocrine tumors. Evidence and approved uses depend on the formulation, with short-acting injections, depot products and other presentations serving different clinical roles.
description: Sandostatin injection is approved for reducing GH and IGF-1 in selected patients with acromegaly, severe diarrhea and flushing associated with metastatic carcinoid tumors, and watery diarrhea from VIP-secreting tumors. Long-acting formulations provide sustained exposure for appropriate patients. Symptom suppression can be valuable even when it does not mean the underlying tumor has disappeared. Octreotide is also studied and used in other specialist settings, but those practices must be distinguished from the specific product label. One formulation’s indication or administration method should never be assumed to apply to every octreotide product.
mechanism: Octreotide binds somatostatin receptors and reproduces many effects of the body’s inhibitory hormone somatostatin. It suppresses GH, insulin, glucagon and several gastrointestinal peptides, and can reduce splanchnic blood flow. These actions explain both control of hormone-mediated diarrhea and important off-target effects on glucose, gallbladder emptying and digestion. Its receptor profile and duration differ from other somatostatin analogs.
keyTakeaway: Octreotide has established disease-specific uses, but controlling hormone symptoms and controlling tumor growth are different objectives. The actual formulation, disease and monitoring plan determine how its evidence applies.

sections.title: Label-specific uses
sections.body: The injectable Sandostatin label emphasizes endocrine and symptom control. It explicitly distinguishes those findings from evidence of tumor shrinkage or slowed growth in its original trials. Other formulations and studies should be evaluated separately.

sections.title: Antiproliferative evidence
sections.body: PROMID evaluated long-acting octreotide in metastatic midgut neuroendocrine tumors and found longer time to tumor progression than placebo. This is evidence for a defined tumor population and formulation, not proof that short-acting octreotide treats all cancers.

sections.title: Important adverse effects
sections.body: Gallstones and their complications, bradycardia, arrhythmias and conduction abnormalities can occur. Insulin and glucagon suppression can produce either high or low glucose. Hypothyroidism and gastrointestinal adverse effects are also recognized.

sections.title: Digestive symptoms during treatment
sections.body: New greasy stools, stool discoloration, loose stools, bloating or weight loss may reflect pancreatic exocrine insufficiency. These symptoms can resemble the underlying gastrointestinal disease, making reassessment important rather than automatically assuming the original illness has worsened.

sections.title: Why formulation matters
sections.body: An immediate-acting injection, long-acting depot and an oral formulation have different absorption and exposure. They are not interchangeable based on the ingredient name alone. The chosen product determines the relevant indication, administration and follow-up instructions.

name: Plecanatide
molecularClass: Uroguanylin analog and GC-C agonist peptide
summary: Plecanatide is an oral peptide that increases intestinal fluid secretion to treat chronic idiopathic constipation and IBS with constipation in adults. It acts locally in the gut, but can cause severe diarrhea and has strict pediatric safety restrictions.
description: Trulance is used for two adult constipation diagnoses: chronic idiopathic constipation and irritable bowel syndrome with constipation. The first centers on persistent difficult or infrequent bowel movements without an identified secondary cause; IBS-C also includes a pattern of abdominal pain. Plecanatide does not treat mechanical obstruction and is not established as a general gut-healing or anti-inflammatory medicine. Its limited systemic absorption is relevant to pharmacology, but the clinically important effect is movement of fluid into the intestine, which can become excessive in susceptible patients.
mechanism: Plecanatide resembles the endogenous peptide uroguanylin and activates guanylate cyclase-C on intestinal epithelial cells. Increased cyclic GMP stimulates chloride and bicarbonate secretion, principally through CFTR, increasing luminal fluid and transit. Animal findings also link extracellular cyclic GMP to reduced pain-nerve activity. Clinical improvement in IBS-C is evaluated by patient symptoms and bowel outcomes rather than that laboratory mechanism alone.
keyTakeaway: Plecanatide is an established adult constipation treatment with a specific local mechanism. Its favorable absorption profile does not remove the need to assess diarrhea, dehydration, obstruction and pediatric restrictions.

sections.title: Two adult indications
sections.body: U.S. labeling covers chronic idiopathic constipation and IBS-C in adults. Safety and effectiveness below age eighteen are not established. Eligibility is based on the constipation diagnosis, not simply a desire to improve digestion or bowel frequency.

sections.title: Clinical trial outcomes
sections.body: A phase 3 placebo-controlled trial in chronic idiopathic constipation assessed sustained complete spontaneous bowel-movement response. Plecanatide improved that endpoint, supporting a measurable bowel-function benefit rather than a claim that it corrects every underlying cause of constipation.

sections.title: Diarrhea and dehydration
sections.body: Diarrhea is the common adverse reaction and can be severe. The label includes a boxed warning for serious dehydration risk in pediatric patients. Minimal measurable drug in the circulation does not prevent dehydration caused by its local intestinal effect.

sections.title: Pediatric and obstruction restrictions
sections.body: Plecanatide is contraindicated below age six and in known or suspected mechanical gastrointestinal obstruction. The label advises avoiding use from six to under eighteen because pediatric safety and effectiveness have not been established.

sections.title: Relationship to linaclotide
sections.body: Both medicines activate intestinal GC-C, but they are different peptides with different product labels. In particular, current linaclotide pediatric approvals should not be transferred to plecanatide merely because the two drugs share a receptor target.

name: Setmelanotide
summary: Setmelanotide targets a central appetite pathway in specific rare forms of obesity. Current U.S. approval includes acquired hypothalamic obesity and defined syndromic or genetic conditions, with different minimum ages. It is not approved for ordinary polygenic obesity.
description: Imcivree is used when a defined disruption of hypothalamic appetite signaling makes MC4 receptor activation an appropriate therapeutic target. The 2026 U.S. label includes acquired hypothalamic obesity from age four, and Bardet-Biedl syndrome or qualifying POMC, PCSK1 or LEPR deficiency from age two. Genetic findings require appropriate interpretation; a benign variant or a commercial genetic result alone is not sufficient. Diagnosis and clinical context distinguish this treatment from broader obesity medicines. Its evidence should therefore be understood in relation to the specific disorder rather than body weight alone.
mechanism: Setmelanotide activates melanocortin-4 receptors in brain pathways regulating hunger, satiety and energy expenditure. It can restore downstream signaling when certain upstream pathways are impaired. Activity at melanocortin-1 receptors explains increased skin pigmentation. This targeted biology is why the medicine can help selected rare disorders while the label does not expect the same effectiveness in unrelated genetic syndromes or general polygenic obesity.
keyTakeaway: Setmelanotide is a precision treatment for specified causes of obesity. The 2026 acquired-hypothalamic-obesity indication is a real expansion, but it does not make the medicine suitable for all obesity.

sections.title: Current indication boundaries
sections.body: Acquired hypothalamic obesity, Bardet-Biedl syndrome and qualifying POMC, PCSK1 or LEPR deficiency are separate labeled groups. The label excludes general polygenic obesity and deficiencies based on variants classified as benign or likely benign.

sections.title: Rare-disease trial evidence
sections.body: Trials in POMC and LEPR deficiency measured body-weight reduction and hunger in small, genetically defined groups. The results support targeted treatment, but small rare-disease cohorts cannot be treated as evidence for the much larger population with common obesity.

sections.title: Pigmentation, mood and sexual effects
sections.body: Generalized darkening of skin, changes in moles and new pigmented lesions require attention. Depression or suicidal thoughts, spontaneous erections and other sexual adverse reactions have occurred. Serious hypersensitivity is possible.

sections.title: Additional considerations in acquired hypothalamic obesity
sections.body: The current label adds attention to acute adrenal insufficiency and sodium disturbances in patients with acquired hypothalamic obesity, especially those with central diabetes insipidus. These problems reflect the broader endocrine consequences of hypothalamic disease.

sections.title: What the diagnosis contributes
sections.body: A specialist assessment connects the clinical syndrome, genetic or structural findings, hunger pattern and other pituitary deficits. The decision is not based on a weight threshold alone, and skin examination and mental-health follow-up remain part of the treatment context.

name: Sincalide
summary: Sincalide is an intravenous diagnostic peptide that contracts the gallbladder and stimulates pancreatic secretion in defined testing settings. It helps clinicians measure digestive-organ function or facilitate imaging; it is not an established treatment for chronic gallbladder disease or general digestive wellness.
description: Kinevac reproduces selected actions of cholecystokinin, the hormone released after food enters the intestine. Its U.S. label includes stimulating gallbladder contraction, pancreatic secretion when used with secretin, and accelerating movement of a barium meal in selected examinations. The resulting response is measured under a diagnostic protocol. Symptoms, imaging findings and test technique determine interpretation. A low or high measured response is not a complete diagnosis on its own, and the same drug can produce different discomfort or gallbladder measurements when the administration protocol changes.
mechanism: The active octapeptide corresponds to the biologically active end of cholecystokinin. It stimulates gallbladder smooth-muscle contraction and pancreatic enzyme secretion, and affects gastrointestinal motility. Those normal digestive responses become a controlled challenge during testing. Contracting a gallbladder that contains stones can also cause stone movement, which is why the diagnostic purpose does not eliminate the possibility of biliary complications.
keyTakeaway: Sincalide is a diagnostic challenge agent with useful but protocol-dependent responses. It should be understood as part of a supervised investigation, not as a gallbladder cleanse or a long-term digestive treatment.

sections.title: Approved diagnostic purposes
sections.body: The label covers gallbladder contraction, pancreatic secretion in conjunction with secretin, and selected barium-meal transit applications in adults. These are procedural uses, not an approval for treating unexplained abdominal pain with repeated peptide exposure.

sections.title: Why administration protocol matters
sections.body: A multicenter investigation of gallbladder ejection-fraction testing compared sincalide infusion approaches and established reference values for a standardized method. The study illustrates that a numeric test result is meaningful only in relation to how the test was performed.

sections.title: Adverse effects and exclusions
sections.body: Abdominal cramping, nausea and other gastrointestinal symptoms can occur. Serious allergic reactions are possible, including reactions related to sulfites in the preparation. Intestinal obstruction and hypersensitivity to sincalide or relevant components are contraindications.

sections.title: Gallstones and pregnancy
sections.body: Gallbladder contraction can dislodge stones and contribute to obstruction. The label also addresses possible pregnancy-related effects because stimulation can affect smooth muscle. These risks belong in the decision to perform the test, not only in interpreting the result.

sections.title: What a test can establish
sections.body: A functional measurement can support a diagnosis when combined with symptoms and structural imaging. It does not by itself demonstrate that surgery, supplements or another particular intervention will resolve a patient’s symptoms.

name: Teduglutide
summary: Teduglutide is an approved intestinal-rehabilitation medicine for short bowel syndrome in patients who depend on parenteral support. It improves absorptive capacity and can reduce support requirements, while requiring surveillance for intestinal growth, obstruction, fluid overload and biliary or pancreatic complications.
description: Gattex is used in adults and children aged one year and older with short bowel syndrome who require parenteral support. The clinical problem is loss of enough functioning bowel to maintain fluid or nutrition without intravenous assistance. Treatment aims to improve absorption and reduce that dependence under specialist management. Some patients become independent of support, but that is not guaranteed, and anatomy and baseline needs influence response. Teduglutide is not approved for routine IBS, nonspecific intestinal permeability, or recovery from ordinary digestive discomfort, despite being described as a gut-directed peptide.
mechanism: Teduglutide activates the GLP-2 receptor and promotes intestinal adaptation, including changes in mucosal growth and absorption. A substitution makes it more resistant to enzymatic breakdown than native GLP-2. Increased absorption can improve fluid and nutrient handling, but can also alter exposure to oral medicines and create fluid overload if parenteral support is not reassessed. Its growth-promoting biology explains the attention to intestinal neoplasia.
keyTakeaway: Teduglutide can reduce the burden of parenteral support in established intestinal failure. Its benefits depend on coordinated nutritional care and surveillance; they should not be generalized into a claim of universal gut repair.

atAGlance.label: Age scope
atAGlance.value: 1 year and older in the U.S.

sections.title: The condition it treats
sections.body: Short bowel syndrome with dependence on parenteral support is the labeled condition. The objective is improved intestinal absorption and reduced support needs, not simply a change in stool frequency or an improvement in a nonspecific digestive symptom score.

sections.title: Reduction in support requirements
sections.body: Clinical trials and their extensions measured reductions in parenteral-support volume and days of support. Some participants achieved enteral autonomy over extended treatment. These outcomes require careful accounting of fluid and nutrition rather than interpreting weight gain alone as recovery.

sections.title: Growth-related and gastrointestinal risks
sections.body: The label warns about possible acceleration of neoplastic growth, intestinal obstruction and gallbladder, biliary or pancreatic disease. Baseline and follow-up gastrointestinal surveillance are part of the treatment framework, with age-specific recommendations.

sections.title: Fluids and other medicines
sections.body: Greater absorption can cause fluid overload or worsen heart failure if support is not adjusted. It can also increase absorption of oral drugs, especially important for medicines with a narrow therapeutic range. Changes or discontinuation require reassessment of fluid and electrolyte balance.

sections.title: Why specialist nutrition care remains necessary
sections.body: A lower prescribed support volume is beneficial only if hydration, kidney function, nutritional status and daily function remain adequate. Teduglutide supports intestinal rehabilitation; it does not replace the ongoing assessment of the remaining bowel and overall nutritional needs.

name: Terlipressin
summary: Terlipressin is a hospital medicine approved in the United States to improve kidney function in adults with rapidly progressive hepatorenal syndrome. Its renal benefit must be weighed against a boxed risk of serious or fatal respiratory failure and other ischemic complications.
description: Hepatorenal syndrome can develop in advanced liver disease when severe circulatory changes impair kidney perfusion. Terlivaz is used for the form with rapid reduction in kidney function, alongside careful management of volume status and the underlying liver disease. It does not repair the liver or establish that transplantation is unnecessary. Benefits are less likely in very advanced renal dysfunction, and treatment-related complications can affect transplant eligibility. Uses in other countries, including some portal-hypertension settings, should be distinguished from the specific U.S. approval and the patient's immediate clinical circumstances.
mechanism: Terlipressin acts at vasopressin receptors and is converted to lysine vasopressin. Vasoconstriction, particularly in the splanchnic circulation, can improve effective circulating volume and renal perfusion in hepatorenal syndrome. The same constrictive effect can compromise coronary, mesenteric or peripheral blood supply. Its actions therefore demand assessment of both the potential kidney response and cardiopulmonary or ischemic vulnerability.
keyTakeaway: Terlipressin can reverse renal dysfunction in some patients with hepatorenal syndrome, but it carries major respiratory and ischemic risks. It is a closely monitored hospital treatment, not general kidney support.

sections.title: The approved indication
sections.body: The U.S. label covers adults with hepatorenal syndrome and rapidly declining kidney function. Patients with serum creatinine above 5 mg/dL are unlikely to benefit, underscoring that severity and timing influence the treatment decision.

sections.title: Benefit and harm in CONFIRM
sections.body: CONFIRM found verified reversal of hepatorenal syndrome in 32% with terlipressin versus 17% with placebo, with albumin strongly recommended in both groups. Respiratory complications were more frequent. Improved renal response did not establish a survival advantage.

sections.title: Respiratory failure warning
sections.body: Volume overload and grade 3 acute-on-chronic liver failure increase respiratory risk. The label requires oxygenation assessment and ongoing monitoring. Existing hypoxia or worsening respiratory symptoms are contraindications.

sections.title: Ischemia and transplant planning
sections.body: Ongoing coronary, peripheral or mesenteric ischemia is a contraindication. Vasoconstriction can produce new ischemic events. A serious adverse reaction may make a listed patient temporarily or permanently ineligible for liver transplantation, so renal response is not the only relevant endpoint.

sections.title: What improvement does not mean
sections.body: A falling creatinine can show a useful hemodynamic response while advanced liver disease remains. Clinical care continues to address infection, volume status, respiratory function and transplant candidacy rather than viewing one improved laboratory value as definitive recovery.

name: Tesamorelin
summary: Tesamorelin is approved for excess abdominal visceral fat in adults with HIV-associated lipodystrophy. It stimulates the GH–IGF-1 axis and is generally weight neutral; use for ordinary obesity, bodybuilding or anti-aging is outside that approved indication.
description: Egrifta formulations contain tesamorelin, a growth hormone-releasing factor analog. The approved population has HIV-associated lipodystrophy with excess abdominal fat, which differs from generalized obesity and from isolated low growth-hormone measurements. Trials measured visceral adipose tissue, not merely body weight. This profile intentionally combines the reference catalog’s standard and off-label tesamorelin listings because they concern the same active molecule. Keeping them together makes the boundary clear: approval of the HIV indication does not establish a favorable benefit-risk balance for general wellness, athletic physique goals or treatment of aging.
mechanism: Tesamorelin binds pituitary GHRH receptors and increases endogenous growth-hormone release, leading to increased IGF-1 and downstream metabolic effects. It therefore requires a responsive hypothalamic-pituitary axis and differs from injecting recombinant GH directly. Visceral-fat reduction can occur without meaningful overall weight loss. Stimulation of this hormonal pathway also explains concerns about glucose tolerance, fluid retention and exposure of susceptible tissues to growth signals.
keyTakeaway: Tesamorelin’s strongest evidence supports HIV-associated excess visceral fat, not general weight loss. Off-label interest does not change the need to consider IGF-1, glucose, malignancy history and the durability of benefit.

sections.title: Approved versus off-label use
sections.body: U.S. labeling limits use to reducing excess abdominal fat in adults with HIV-associated lipodystrophy and states that tesamorelin is not indicated for weight-loss management. Its long-term cardiovascular safety has not been established.

sections.title: What randomized trials demonstrated
sections.body: A placebo-controlled trial showed reductions in visceral adipose tissue and improvements in body-image distress. During the extension, visceral-fat benefit was maintained with continued treatment and rapidly lost after switching to placebo. A response therefore does not imply permanent remodeling.

sections.title: Growth-factor and metabolic risks
sections.body: Elevated IGF-1, glucose intolerance or diabetes, fluid retention, joint symptoms, carpal-tunnel-type symptoms and hypersensitivity are important concerns. Active malignancy, pregnancy and disruption of the hypothalamic-pituitary axis are contraindications.

sections.title: What a meaningful response includes
sections.body: IGF-1 and glucose require assessment in addition to body composition. A change in abdominal appearance should be balanced against metabolic adverse effects and the reason for treatment. Egrifta formulations have different preparation characteristics and are not interchangeable solely by volume.

sections.title: Why the off-label listing is merged
sections.body: The molecule is the same when marketed for wellness, but the patient population and evidence are different. Combining the records avoids duplicate knowledge and makes it possible to explain approved HIV-related care and unapproved general-wellness claims in one evidence-based account.

sections.title: Common questions
sections.body:
Does tesamorelin treat ordinary obesity? Its FDA indication is reduction of excess abdominal fat in adults with HIV-associated lipodystrophy. That does not establish general obesity treatment.

Is the fat reduction permanent? Extension studies found that visceral fat tended to return after treatment stopped. The decision to continue therefore involves both demonstrated response and ongoing metabolic and growth-factor safety assessment.

name: Retatrutide
molecularClass: Triple GIP, GLP-1 and glucagon receptor agonist peptide
summary: Retatrutide is an investigational triple-receptor metabolic peptide with substantial weight-loss effects in randomized trials, including phase 3 results. It remains distinct from approved semaglutide and tirzepatide products; trial efficacy does not establish an approved retail product or long-term outcomes for every population.
description: Developed as LY3437943, retatrutide combines GIP, GLP-1 and glucagon receptor activity in one molecule. Its clinical program evaluates obesity and associated metabolic complications. The 2026 TRIUMPH-1 publication extends the evidence beyond the earlier phase 2 study, including outcomes in participants with knee osteoarthritis or obstructive sleep apnea. These findings come from regulated studies using controlled manufacturing and follow-up. Products sold online under the same name are not the studied product by default. As of this review, the ingredient remains investigational rather than an FDA-approved weight-management medicine.
mechanism: GIP and GLP-1 activity influence glucose-dependent insulin secretion and appetite, while glucagon receptor activity adds effects on hepatic metabolism and energy expenditure. The design balances pathways that do not have identical effects on glucose or food intake. Calling it a triple agonist describes receptor pharmacology; it does not establish that three targets are always safer or clinically superior to two for an individual patient.
keyTakeaway: Retatrutide has progressed to compelling phase 3 evidence, but remains an investigational medicine at this review date. Efficacy, regulatory approval, manufacturing quality and long-term safety are separate questions.

sections.title: Conditions under investigation
sections.body: The program studies obesity and associated conditions rather than a nonspecific wellness effect. TRIUMPH-1 included adults with obesity without diabetes and prospectively assessed weight and selected knee-osteoarthritis and sleep-apnea outcomes.

sections.title: What the 2026 phase 3 study found
sections.body: Across 2,339 randomized participants, the highest trial group had a mean 25.0% weight reduction at eighty weeks versus 3.9% with placebo in the treatment-regimen analysis. Pain and sleep-apnea outcomes also improved in relevant subgroups. These are group averages under a specified estimand.

sections.title: Observed tolerability and remaining uncertainty
sections.body: Gastrointestinal adverse events were common. The earlier phase 2 trial also observed dose-related heart-rate increases that peaked and later declined. Larger trials improve confidence but cannot fully characterize rare events or risks after many years of use.

sections.title: Why headline percentages can mislead
sections.body: Phase 2 and phase 3 studies differed in duration, participants and analysis. Comparing their percentages with another drug’s separate trial is not equivalent to a randomized head-to-head comparison. Discontinuation handling also affects reported weight-loss estimates.

sections.title: Trial evidence versus approved access
sections.body: FDA communications identify retatrutide among unapproved products marketed for weight loss. A research-use label, compounded presentation or online certificate does not turn an investigational molecule into an approved medicine or validate a seller’s clinical claims.

sections.title: Common questions
sections.body:
Does a positive phase 3 trial mean retatrutide is approved? No. Trial results and regulatory authorization are separate milestones, and the current FDA source identifies it as unapproved.

Can its headline weight loss be directly compared with another medicine's trial? Differences in populations, duration and handling of discontinuation can change estimates; direct comparative studies provide stronger evidence for treatment rankings.

name: Cagrilintide
summary: Cagrilintide is an investigational amylin analog developed for weight management, both alone and with semaglutide. Human trials support appetite-related weight reduction, but the single agent and the CagriSema combination have different evidence and cannot be treated as interchangeable products.
description: Amylin is a pancreatic hormone involved in meal-related satiety. Cagrilintide extends that signaling approach through a long-acting engineered peptide. A phase 2 monotherapy study established dose-related weight reduction in adults without diabetes, and later combination trials studied cagrilintide alongside semaglutide. Those programs ask different questions: one tests amylin-based treatment by itself, the other combines amylin and GLP-1 activity. A favorable combination result cannot simply be assigned to cagrilintide alone. The current knowledge base therefore retains separate canonical records for cagrilintide and the two-drug combination.
mechanism: Cagrilintide engages amylin-related receptor signaling, including receptor complexes formed from calcitonin receptors and receptor-activity-modifying proteins. These pathways influence satiation and food intake through brain circuits distinct from, but overlapping functionally with, GLP-1 signaling. Its prolonged activity supports investigation as a weekly injection. The intended mechanism is pharmacologic appetite regulation; it is not replacement for a diagnosed general amylin-deficiency syndrome.
keyTakeaway: Cagrilintide has credible human weight-management evidence, yet remains investigational. Standalone results, combination results and an eventual product label must remain distinct when assessing benefit and safety.

sections.title: What is being developed
sections.body: Monotherapy trials examine weight management in eligible adults. Combination development adds semaglutide to target another appetite pathway. These are pharmacologically related strategies but do not have identical exposure, trial populations or tolerability.

sections.title: Monotherapy evidence
sections.body: The phase 2 trial enrolled 706 adults and followed treatment for twenty-six weeks. Cagrilintide produced greater mean weight reduction than placebo, with gastrointestinal and administration-site events commonly reported. The study supported further development rather than establishing long-term cardiovascular benefit.

sections.title: What combination studies add
sections.body: REDEFINE 1 included separate cagrilintide, semaglutide, combination and placebo groups. That design helps distinguish each component from the combination. The larger average combination effect should not be advertised as the expected result from cagrilintide alone.

sections.title: What is known and still unknown
sections.body: Nausea, constipation, diarrhea and injection-site reactions appeared in monotherapy research. Longer and larger studies are needed to clarify uncommon harms, durability and use in populations not represented in early trials. A positive short-term tolerability assessment is not proof of unrestricted safety.

sections.title: Current status and product identity
sections.body: Cagrilintide remains investigational in the sources reviewed. FDA has specifically cautioned about unapproved weight-loss products containing it. Trial registration and a commercial research listing do not establish marketing approval or confirm the contents of a purchased product.

sections.title: Common questions
sections.body:
Is cagrilintide a GLP-1 medicine? It is an amylin-pathway agonist; semaglutide supplies the GLP-1 component in CagriSema.

Can CagriSema results be attributed entirely to cagrilintide? No. Combination studies assess the combined regimen and its comparators. Cagrilintide monotherapy has its own evidence, and its independent effect should be taken from the appropriate study arm rather than the combination's headline result.

name: Amycretin
molecularClass: Unimolecular GLP-1 and amylin receptor agonist peptide
summary: Amycretin, now also known as zenagamtide, is an investigational peptide combining GLP-1 and amylin-related receptor activity in one molecule. Oral and injectable programs have shown metabolic effects in human trials, but their formulations, endpoints and evidence maturity differ.
description: Amycretin was the development name used in early studies of this single-molecule approach; 2026 research uses the name zenagamtide. The compound is distinct from CagriSema, which combines two separate active peptides. Both oral and subcutaneous formulations have entered clinical studies. Early obesity studies emphasized safety, exposure and exploratory weight change, while a 2026 oral phase 2 trial assessed glycated hemoglobin in type 2 diabetes. These different designs should not be collapsed into one promised weight-loss percentage or an assertion of established cardiovascular protection.
mechanism: The molecule activates GLP-1 and amylin-related signaling, with calcitonin receptor activity also described in the phase 2 publication. The goal is to combine glucose-regulating and satiety effects within one peptide rather than administering separate drugs. Delivery changes exposure: an oral peptide formulation must overcome gastrointestinal degradation and absorption barriers, so injectable and oral study results cannot be translated by comparing nominal amounts.
keyTakeaway: Amycretin/zenagamtide is a substantive clinical-development program, not an approved treatment at this review date. Its oral and injectable evidence should be read separately, with attention to study size and endpoints.

sections.title: What the trials investigate
sections.body: Development targets weight management and glucose control. The oral type 2 diabetes trial studied adults already receiving metformin with or without an SGLT2 inhibitor, so its results do not establish use in untreated diabetes or type 1 diabetes.

sections.title: Oral diabetes evidence
sections.body: In the 2026 phase 2 trial, 186 participants were randomized and followed for thirty-six weeks. Oral zenagamtide lowered HbA1c more than placebo across tested groups. The primary question was glycemic efficacy, not cardiovascular events or long-term obesity complications.

sections.title: Injectable obesity evidence
sections.body: The phase 1b/2a study included 125 participants across several cohorts and reported substantial exploratory weight reduction. A high number withdrew, including many for reasons unrelated to adverse events. Small cohorts and missing-data assumptions limit certainty around headline percentages.

sections.title: Tolerability and evidence gaps
sections.body: Gastrointestinal events predominated in oral and injectable studies. Early trials cannot reliably exclude uncommon or delayed harms. Pregnancy, pediatric use, combination with other appetite medicines and long-term outcomes require dedicated evidence rather than extrapolation from receptor targets.

sections.title: Is this the same as CagriSema?
sections.body: No. Amycretin/zenagamtide is one engineered molecule, while CagriSema uses cagrilintide plus semaglutide. Similar therapeutic concepts do not mean identical pharmacology, exposure, safety or regulatory status.

name: Apraglutide
summary: Apraglutide is an investigational GLP-2 analog for short bowel syndrome with intestinal failure. A phase 3 trial showed reduced parenteral-support volume, but regulatory development continues, including an additional confirmatory study; it is not an approved substitute for teduglutide.
description: Apraglutide is designed to improve intestinal adaptation and absorption in people who need intravenous fluid or nutrition because too little functioning bowel remains. Its long action supports investigation as a weekly treatment. The STARS trial evaluated patients with different intestinal anatomies, including a stoma or colon in continuity. Not every secondary endpoint was positive, and treatment response cannot be inferred from the overall trial average alone. In 2025 the FDA requested another confirmatory phase 3 study, and the sponsor’s 2026 plans include STARS-2. This distinguishes demonstrated trial activity from a completed approval process.
mechanism: Apraglutide activates the GLP-2 receptor, supporting intestinal mucosal adaptation and absorptive function. Longer exposure is intended to reduce administration frequency relative to shorter-acting GLP-2 therapy. Increased uptake of fluid and nutrients may reduce parenteral-support requirements, but must be balanced against changing hydration needs. A trophic intestinal mechanism also creates questions about obstruction, abnormal tissue growth and long-term gastrointestinal surveillance that clinical development must resolve.
keyTakeaway: Apraglutide has phase 3 evidence for reducing parenteral support in intestinal failure, but confirmatory development remains necessary. Its clinical goal is measurable nutritional independence or reduced support, not nonspecific digestive enhancement.

sections.title: The population being studied
sections.body: The development program concerns short bowel syndrome with dependence on parenteral support. It does not test routine IBS or generalized gut-health claims, and anatomy-specific analyses help explain why responses may differ across patients.

sections.title: STARS primary result
sections.body: In 163 randomized and treated patients, weekly support volume fell by a mean 25.5% with apraglutide versus 12.5% with placebo at week twenty-four. More treated patients achieved at least one fewer support day per week at that time.

sections.title: Secondary outcomes require nuance
sections.body: In the colon-in-continuity group at week forty-eight, differences in days off support and enteral autonomy were not statistically significant. A positive primary endpoint therefore does not establish that all clinically desirable outcomes were achieved.

sections.title: What remains under evaluation
sections.body: The trial reported a generally favorable tolerability profile, but the size and duration limit detection of uncommon harms. Long-term consequences of intestinal growth and changing fluid absorption remain relevant to the benefit-risk assessment of GLP-2-directed treatment.

sections.title: Why a positive study is not approval
sections.body: Ironwood’s regulatory update states that FDA requested an additional confirmatory phase 3 study. Its 2026 update describes STARS-2. Apraglutide remains investigational, and the existence of an approved GLP-2 analog does not confer approval on this separate molecule.

name: Brilacidin
summary: Brilacidin is an investigational small molecule designed to mimic host-defense peptides, rather than a peptide itself. It has been studied in infections, oral mucositis and localized ulcerative colitis, with laboratory antiviral findings that should not be confused with proven clinical treatment benefit.
description: Brilacidin’s inclusion in peptide catalogs reflects its design inspiration, not its chemical identity. The compound was engineered to reproduce selected properties of defensins and other host-defense molecules while using a nonpeptide scaffold. Its clinical studies have used different delivery approaches, including intravenous administration, oral rinse and local intestinal administration. Each route and condition creates a separate evidence question. Activity against a virus in a cell culture does not validate an intravenous treatment for viral disease, and a small local colitis study does not establish a general treatment for inflammatory bowel disease.
mechanism: Experimental work describes interactions with microbial membranes and host-cell attachment pathways. In coronavirus cell models, brilacidin disrupted viral integrity and affected entry, including interactions involving cell-surface heparan sulfate proteoglycans. Anti-inflammatory effects are also part of its development rationale. These mechanisms depend on experimental concentration, exposure and model; their presence alone does not prove that a safe human regimen reaches the required target effect.
keyTakeaway: Brilacidin belongs in the catalog as a defensin mimetic with clinical research history, while being clearly labeled nonpeptide and investigational. Evidence must be evaluated separately for each condition and route.

sections.title: Human development programs
sections.body: The sponsor describes clinical studies in acute bacterial skin infections, oral mucositis and ulcerative proctitis or proctosigmoiditis. These differ in disease severity, exposure and outcome measures, so one program cannot establish another indication.

sections.title: What antiviral experiments show
sections.body: Studies in lung and other cell lines found inhibition of SARS-CoV-2 and several human coronaviruses. Those experiments support mechanistic research. They do not measure hospitalization, recovery, mortality or clinically achievable benefit in a patient.

sections.title: Clinical findings require their own assessment
sections.body: The COVID-19 program proceeded to a randomized phase 2 study. A sponsor update discussed disappointing topline findings and further analysis. Laboratory potency should not be used to override a clinical trial’s actual primary endpoint or to claim an approved antiviral indication.

sections.title: Route-specific uncertainty
sections.body: Safety observed with a local rinse or enema does not establish safety after systemic administration. The investigational record does not provide a generally approved dosing, interaction or long-term safety framework for unsupervised use across the proposed diseases.

sections.title: Designations are not approval
sections.body: Fast Track or Qualified Infectious Disease Product designations can support development, but do not authorize routine marketing as an effective medicine. Brilacidin remains a development compound in the primary sources reviewed.

name: CagriSema
molecularClass: Combination of an amylin analog and a GLP-1 receptor agonist
summary: CagriSema combines cagrilintide and semaglutide in an investigational weight-management treatment. Phase 3 studies demonstrate substantial weight reduction, but combination efficacy, adverse effects and pending regulatory review are separate from the existing approvals of semaglutide products.
description: CagriSema is a combination of two active peptides, rather than a new generic name for semaglutide alone. Cagrilintide adds amylin-related appetite signaling to semaglutide’s GLP-1 effects. The REDEFINE program has studied adults with obesity or overweight, including separate populations with and without type 2 diabetes. The sponsor filed a U.S. application in December 2025 and reported continued review during 2026. As of this review date, the combination is not treated as an approved medicine. Manufacturing or mixing the components outside the studied product does not reproduce the trial evidence automatically.
mechanism: Semaglutide activates GLP-1 receptors and influences appetite, glucose-dependent insulin secretion and gastric emptying. Cagrilintide provides prolonged amylin-related receptor activity affecting satiation. Combining the pathways aims to improve weight reduction beyond either component alone, but also combines pharmacologic burdens, especially gastrointestinal effects. The net result must be demonstrated in clinical trials rather than inferred solely from having two mechanisms.
keyTakeaway: CagriSema has strong phase 3 weight-loss evidence but remained under regulatory review at the cutoff. Its results should be attributed to the combination and population studied, with uncertainty about long-term outcomes kept explicit.

sections.title: Which populations were studied
sections.body: REDEFINE 1 enrolled adults with obesity or qualifying overweight without diabetes. REDEFINE 2 addressed overweight or obesity with type 2 diabetes. Different baseline physiology and treatments mean that results from one population do not predict identical effects in the other.

sections.title: Phase 3 efficacy
sections.body: REDEFINE 1 randomized 3,417 participants. In the treatment-policy analysis, mean weight change at sixty-eight weeks was −20.4% with the combination and −3.0% with placebo. The trial also included individual-component groups, allowing direct evaluation within that study.

sections.title: Gastrointestinal burden
sections.body: Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, constipation and abdominal pain were frequent in REDEFINE 1, usually transient and mild to moderate. A mean weight-loss benefit must be considered alongside discontinuation, tolerability and the practical ability to continue therapy.

sections.title: Head-to-head evidence
sections.body: The sponsor reported that REDEFINE 4 did not meet its primary noninferiority objective against tirzepatide. This directly comparative finding matters more than ranking drugs from unrelated trials with different durations and statistical analyses.

sections.title: Semaglutide approval does not approve the combination
sections.body: The sponsor’s 2026 filing states that the combination’s U.S. application was submitted in December 2025. Existing semaglutide approvals do not extend automatically to cagrilintide or CagriSema, and a pending application is not a final marketing authorization.

sections.title: Common questions
sections.body:
Does Wegovy approval also approve CagriSema? No. Adding cagrilintide produces a different investigational combination that needs its own regulatory assessment.

Did every comparison favor CagriSema? No. Although placebo-controlled phase 3 studies demonstrated substantial weight loss, the sponsor reported that REDEFINE 4 did not meet its primary noninferiority comparison with tirzepatide. That distinction belongs alongside the positive results.
