name: Pramlintide
summary: Pramlintide is an approved adjunct to mealtime insulin for selected adults with type 1 or type 2 diabetes. It complements insulin’s actions but increases the risk of severe hypoglycemia, especially in type 1 diabetes, and is not an approved standalone obesity medicine.
description: Symlin replaces selected actions of amylin, a hormone normally released with insulin from pancreatic beta cells. Its indication concerns people using mealtime insulin who have not achieved desired glycemic control despite optimized insulin treatment. The therapy adds complexity because meals, insulin exposure, glucose monitoring and gastric emptying all interact. The label emphasizes careful patient selection and trained diabetes follow-up. This is a distinct clinical role from newer long-acting amylin analogs being developed for obesity. Their mechanism-related relationship does not permit transfer of approvals, administration practices or safety assumptions.
mechanism: Pramlintide slows gastric emptying, suppresses inappropriate post-meal glucagon secretion and promotes satiety. These actions reduce the rate at which glucose enters the circulation after meals and complement the glucose-disposal effect of insulin. Because carbohydrate appearance and insulin action can become mismatched, adding pramlintide without an appropriate prescribing plan can cause severe hypoglycemia. Delayed gastric emptying can also affect oral-drug absorption.
keyTakeaway: Pramlintide is an established but selective adjunct to insulin, requiring coordinated glucose management. Its amylin mechanism does not make it an interchangeable weight-loss peptide or eliminate the risks of concomitant insulin.

sections.title: Who the label describes
sections.body: The indication includes type 1 or type 2 diabetes with mealtime insulin when desired control remains unmet despite optimal insulin therapy. The label stresses suitability, reliable monitoring and access to experienced diabetes care.

sections.title: What clinical benefit is measured
sections.body: Registration studies assessed additional glycemic improvement with insulin-based treatment, along with body-weight effects. A weight change in diabetes trials does not establish an independent obesity indication or demonstrate long-term cardiovascular benefit.

sections.title: Hypoglycemia and nausea
sections.body: Severe hypoglycemia is the major boxed risk, particularly in type 1 diabetes. Nausea is common. Reduced awareness of low glucose and confirmed gastroparesis are contraindications, because they increase the difficulty or danger of coordinating treatment with meals and insulin.

sections.title: Why it is kept separate from insulin
sections.body: The label prohibits mixing pramlintide and insulin in the same injection because this can alter pharmacokinetics. It also addresses oral medicines for which prompt absorption or a threshold concentration is important, given delayed gastric emptying.

sections.title: Relationship to investigational amylin drugs
sections.body: Cagrilintide and petrelintide are different long-acting analogs with separate obesity-development programs. Pramlintide’s approval does not approve those molecules, and their trial results do not establish a new indication for Symlin.

name: Secretin
molecularClass: Synthetic human secretin diagnostic peptide hormone
summary: Secretin is an approved diagnostic hormone used to stimulate pancreatic or gastrin secretion during selected tests and procedures. It helps evaluate pancreatic exocrine function, investigate gastrinoma and identify pancreatic duct openings; it is not routine treatment for digestive insufficiency.
description: ChiRhoStim supplies synthetic human secretin, a hormone normally involved in the response to acidic intestinal contents. Its diagnostic value comes from provoking a measurable pancreatic or gastrin response. The product can assist pancreatic exocrine-function assessment, gastrinoma evaluation and identification of the ampulla or accessory papilla during ERCP. These uses depend on technique and clinical context. The current label cautions that medicines and underlying conditions can blunt or exaggerate responses, so an abnormal result should not be interpreted without understanding how the test was prepared, performed and measured.
mechanism: Secretin stimulates pancreatic duct cells to release bicarbonate-rich fluid, helping neutralize acidic contents entering the intestine. Receptor signaling opens pathways including CFTR-mediated secretion, with neural contributions also described. In gastrinoma, an abnormal gastrin response can become a diagnostic signal. The hormone therefore acts as a controlled physiologic stimulus; the measurement and interpretation, not lasting hormone replacement, are the purpose of the approved procedure.
keyTakeaway: Secretin is useful in specific diagnostic pathways when test conditions are controlled. A stimulated secretion measurement does not independently diagnose every pancreatic disorder or establish a therapeutic role for repeated secretin administration.

sections.title: Approved diagnostic applications
sections.body: The label covers stimulation of pancreatic secretion to aid diagnosis of exocrine dysfunction, stimulation of gastrin to aid gastrinoma diagnosis, and pancreatic secretion to help locate duct openings during ERCP.

sections.title: Technique is part of the test
sections.body: Label-described studies compared synthetic and biologically derived secretin preparations and assessed pancreatic responses. The label notes variation between investigators and laboratories, so reference values and operator proficiency matter to interpretation.

sections.title: Adverse effects observed during testing
sections.body: In the label-described open-label trial of 531 patients, reported reactions included nausea, vomiting, flushing and upset stomach. Most patients received a single administration. These observations characterize diagnostic exposure and do not establish the safety of repeated administration for unapproved therapeutic purposes.

sections.title: Medication-related diagnostic errors
sections.body: Anticholinergic medicines can blunt pancreatic response. Proton-pump inhibitors and H2 blockers can alter gastrin responses and falsely suggest gastrinoma. Test preparation should follow the supervising clinician’s plan rather than unsupervised withdrawal of necessary medicines.

sections.title: Underlying disease can distort response
sections.body: Prior vagotomy or inflammatory bowel disease can reduce responses, while alcoholic or other liver disease may increase pancreatic secretion enough to mask coexisting pancreatic disease. Additional clinical assessment can therefore be necessary even after a technically completed test.

sections.title: Diagnostic secretion is not pancreatic replacement
sections.body: Secretin briefly stimulates a response for measurement or visualization. It does not supply digestive enzymes, restore destroyed pancreatic tissue or establish treatment for chronic abdominal symptoms. Those clinical goals require separate evidence and evaluation.

name: Somapacitan
summary: Somapacitan is a long-acting growth-hormone analog used for adult GH deficiency and specified pediatric growth disorders. Current U.S. labeling extends beyond pediatric GH deficiency to selected small-for-gestational-age, Noonan syndrome and idiopathic short-stature populations from age two and a half.
description: Sogroya provides prolonged GH activity through a modified molecule that binds albumin. Its adult indication is replacement in established growth-hormone deficiency. The current pediatric label includes growth failure from inadequate GH secretion, certain children born small for gestational age without catch-up growth, Noonan syndrome and idiopathic short stature. These are defined clinical diagnoses, not a general indication to increase height or improve body composition in otherwise healthy people. Weekly administration changes convenience and exposure patterns, but does not remove the endocrine evaluation, growth assessment or safety surveillance required for GH-directed treatment.
mechanism: Somapacitan activates GH receptors in target tissues and stimulates downstream effects, including IGF-1 production. Reversible albumin binding prolongs exposure compared with unmodified somatropin. Some actions are mediated through IGF-1, while others reflect direct GH signaling. Because concentrations and IGF-1 vary across the weekly interval, the timing of biochemical assessment matters when interpreting response and avoiding excessive hormonal exposure.
keyTakeaway: Somapacitan is established long-acting GH therapy for labeled deficiencies and growth conditions. Its expanded pediatric scope should be recognized, while healthy-adult anti-aging and unrestricted height-enhancement claims remain outside that evidence.

sections.title: Current approved populations
sections.body: The 2026 label includes pediatric GH deficiency, selected SGA short stature, Noonan syndrome and idiopathic short stature from age 2.5, plus adult GH deficiency. The actual diagnostic criteria and growth-plate status determine eligibility.

sections.title: How adult and pediatric benefit differ
sections.body: The adult REAL-1 study evaluated body-composition and metabolic effects in GH deficiency. Pediatric studies assess annualized height velocity and growth outcomes against daily somatropin. Adult fat-mass findings and childhood linear growth are not interchangeable endpoints.

sections.title: GH-related adverse effects
sections.body: Fluid retention, glucose intolerance, intracranial hypertension and thyroid or adrenal-axis changes require attention. Pediatric monitoring includes hip or knee pain suggesting slipped capital femoral epiphysis and progression of scoliosis. Hypersensitivity can occur.

sections.title: Important restrictions
sections.body: Active malignancy, certain acute critical illnesses, severe diabetic retinopathy and closed growth plates for pediatric growth promotion are contraindications. Specific respiratory-risk restrictions apply to children with Prader-Willi syndrome, although that syndrome is not a general Sogroya growth indication.

sections.title: Weekly GH is not a direct volume substitution
sections.body: Long-acting GH analogs differ from daily somatropin and from each other. Their exposure patterns and IGF-1 interpretation are product-specific, so a change in formulation requires a clinical plan rather than simple conversion by injection volume.

name: Somatropin (rhGH)
summary: Somatropin is recombinant human growth hormone with established, product-specific indications in GH deficiency and selected growth or wasting conditions. It is not an approved general anti-aging treatment, and excess exposure can cause metabolic, fluid-retention and growth-related complications.
description: Somatropin products supply a recombinant form of human GH. Several brands treat pediatric growth disorders and adult GH deficiency, while specialized products have other indications: Serostim treats HIV-associated wasting, and Zorbtive has a short-bowel-syndrome indication. Those indications belong to the relevant product labels rather than every somatropin presentation. In children, diagnosis, remaining growth potential and exclusion of alternative causes determine treatment. In adults, a symptom such as fatigue or an age-related decline in a hormone measurement is not by itself established GH deficiency. The full endocrine context matters.
mechanism: Somatropin activates GH receptors and stimulates IGF-1 production, affecting linear growth, protein synthesis, lipid metabolism and body composition. It also has direct metabolic actions, including reduced insulin sensitivity in some settings. Replacing deficient hormone can be beneficial, but pharmacologic excess is biologically different from replacement. The same growth signaling that supports treatment explains concerns about tumor activity and inappropriate use after growth plates have closed.
keyTakeaway: Somatropin is a family of established hormone medicines with product-specific uses. Deficiency treatment, pediatric growth care, HIV wasting and short-bowel therapy should remain distinct from unsupported healthy-adult rejuvenation claims.

sections.title: Approval depends on the product
sections.body: Genotropin covers adult GH deficiency and specified pediatric disorders. Serostim covers adult HIV wasting with antiretroviral therapy. Zorbtive’s short-bowel indication is another distinct use. Sharing somatropin does not make every branded indication interchangeable.

sections.title: What meaningful response looks like
sections.body: Pediatric care assesses height velocity and growth potential; adult replacement evaluates deficiency-related clinical and biochemical outcomes. In HIV wasting, body weight, lean mass and physical endurance are relevant. A higher IGF-1 alone is not a universal measure of improved health.

sections.title: Important adverse effects
sections.body: Edema, joint or muscle symptoms, carpal-tunnel-type symptoms, glucose intolerance and intracranial hypertension can occur. Treatment may reveal or alter thyroid and adrenal deficits. Pediatric monitoring also addresses slipped capital femoral epiphysis and scoliosis progression.

sections.title: Malignancy and critical illness
sections.body: Active malignancy, certain acute critical illnesses and severe diabetic retinopathy are important contraindications. Growth promotion is inappropriate after epiphyseal closure. Specific airway and respiratory restrictions apply in Prader-Willi syndrome because of reported sudden deaths in high-risk children.

sections.title: Why wellness claims require separate evidence
sections.body: The benefits of replacing a deficient hormone do not establish benefits from raising it above physiological need. Approved disease-specific experience cannot be converted into a claim that somatropin prolongs life or safely improves appearance in healthy adults.

name: Efpeglenatide
molecularClass: Long-acting exendin-based GLP-1 receptor agonist conjugate
summary: Efpeglenatide is a long-acting GLP-1 receptor agonist with cardiovascular and kidney-outcome evidence in high-risk type 2 diabetes. South Korea approved an efpeglenatide product for weight management in October 2026; that authorization is distinct from FDA approval and from the earlier diabetes trial population.
description: The efpeglenatide development program spans different clinical questions. AMPLITUDE-O tested cardiovascular and renal outcomes in people with type 2 diabetes and substantial baseline risk. Separately, South Korea’s Ministry of Food and Drug Safety announced approval of an efpeglenatide auto-injector on 7 October 2026 for chronic weight management in eligible adults without diabetes, alongside diet and exercise. The catalog reflects this current approval rather than retaining an outdated globally investigational label. However, the jurisdiction and population must remain explicit: Korean obesity authorization does not mean the FDA has approved efpeglenatide or that every trial finding is a labeled claim.
mechanism: Efpeglenatide uses an exendin-based GLP-1 agonist linked to a carrier system that extends its action. GLP-1 receptor activation influences appetite, gastric emptying, glucose-dependent insulin secretion and glucagon regulation. Those metabolic mechanisms support development in diabetes and obesity, while cardiovascular and kidney benefits require direct outcomes evidence. A shared GLP-1 target alone would not establish the specific results observed in AMPLITUDE-O.
keyTakeaway: Efpeglenatide now has a South Korean obesity approval and a substantial diabetes outcomes-trial history. Keep those two evidence contexts separate, and do not translate a national authorization into universal approval or availability.

sections.title: Current Korean authorization
sections.body: MFDS states that the efpeglenatide auto-injector was approved on 7 October 2026 for chronic weight management in adults with obesity or qualifying overweight without diabetes, used with dietary and exercise measures.

sections.title: Cardiovascular and renal trial results
sections.body: AMPLITUDE-O randomized 4,076 participants with type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular disease or kidney disease plus additional risk. Major cardiovascular events occurred less often with efpeglenatide, and a prespecified renal composite also improved relative to placebo.

sections.title: Different populations answer different questions
sections.body: The outcome trial involved high-risk diabetes, while the new Korean obesity authorization concerns adults without diabetes. The favorable trial result should not be automatically described as the approved prevention claim for every obesity patient.

sections.title: Observed adverse effects
sections.body: Diarrhea, constipation, nausea, vomiting and bloating were more frequent than placebo in AMPLITUDE-O. Current local product information governs contraindications, monitoring and interactions for the approved preparation; the older trial report is not a complete prescribing label.

sections.title: Why an older trial-only label is incomplete
sections.body: Regulatory status changes over time. This record includes the new Korean authorization while retaining the lack of identified FDA approval. Neither label should erase the other jurisdiction’s status or imply immediate commercial access everywhere.

name: Elamipretide
summary: Elamipretide is an FDA-approved medicine for improving muscle strength in patients with Barth syndrome who weigh at least thirty kilograms. The September 2025 accelerated approval is narrow and conditional; it does not establish a general anti-aging, fatigue or mitochondrial-optimization treatment.
description: Forzinity contains elamipretide, previously known as SS-31 or MTP-131. Barth syndrome is a rare mitochondrial disorder linked to abnormal cardiolipin biology. The FDA granted accelerated approval based on improvement in knee-extensor muscle strength, an intermediate clinical endpoint. The evidence history requires nuance: the small randomized study did not show superiority on its primary walking-distance and fatigue endpoints, while longer open-label follow-up supported the strength finding used for approval. This profile therefore updates older research-only classifications without overstating the certainty or breadth of the clinical benefit.
mechanism: Elamipretide localizes to the inner mitochondrial membrane and binds cardiolipin, a lipid important to mitochondrial structure and function. The approved label describes improvement in mitochondrial morphology and function. This mechanism is relevant to Barth syndrome’s biology, but a mitochondrial target is not evidence that treatment improves every condition associated with fatigue, aging or reduced energy production. Clinical indication and molecular mechanism must be distinguished.
keyTakeaway: Elamipretide has a real but narrowly scoped accelerated FDA approval. Confirmatory clinical benefit remains important, and the Barth-syndrome evidence should not be generalized to wellness or unrestricted mitochondrial disease treatment.

sections.title: The approved indication
sections.body: Forzinity is indicated to improve muscle strength in adults and children with Barth syndrome who weigh at least thirty kilograms. It is not a general approval for primary mitochondrial myopathy, ordinary fatigue or longevity enhancement.

sections.title: Why the evidence is conditional
sections.body: The randomized trial enrolled twelve participants and did not meet its primary walking-distance or fatigue endpoints. Muscle-strength improvement emerged during the open-label extension. The label explicitly bases accelerated approval on the intermediate strength endpoint and requires confirmatory benefit assessment.

sections.title: What longer follow-up adds
sections.body: The published extension described sustained changes in functional and cardiac assessments among a very small number of participants. Without a concurrent blinded control group, these findings are informative but more vulnerable to bias than a successful randomized comparison.

sections.title: Important precautions
sections.body: Injection-site reactions are common, and serious hypersensitivity can occur. The formulation contains benzyl alcohol and is not approved for neonates. Kidney impairment affects the labeled treatment considerations; the actual prescription product’s information governs use.

sections.title: Does approval validate SS-31 sold online?
sections.body: No. Approval applies to the regulated Forzinity product and its defined indication. A research product using the SS-31 name does not inherit the approved manufacturing standard or demonstrate equivalent composition, exposure or clinical benefit.

name: MOTS-c
aliases: Mitochondrial open reading frame of the 12S rRNA-c
summary: MOTS-c is a mitochondrial-derived peptide studied in metabolic signaling and physical-function research. Experiments show effects in cells and mice, while observations of endogenous changes during human exercise do not establish that administering MOTS-c improves human health, performance or longevity.
description: The name refers to a short open reading frame associated with mitochondrial 12S rRNA. Discovery studies investigated its role in communication between mitochondrial metabolism and cellular responses. Later work reported better physical performance in treated mice and increased endogenous MOTS-c after exercise in people. These are different types of evidence: measuring a naturally occurring response in humans is not a treatment trial. FDA’s 2026 evaluation found major gaps in human exposure, pharmacokinetics and toxicology for proposed MOTS-c products. It remains a research compound rather than an approved metabolic or anti-aging medicine.
mechanism: The original research linked MOTS-c to changes in the folate cycle and purine synthesis, leading to AMPK-related metabolic signaling. Subsequent work explored nuclear gene regulation, muscle stress responses and metabolic adaptation. The precise molecular target remains incompletely defined. These pathways offer a biological hypothesis, but do not demonstrate that injected peptide reaches sustained active concentrations in human tissues or reproduces the effects of exercise.
keyTakeaway: MOTS-c is scientifically interesting mitochondrial signaling research, with a large gap between mouse treatment results and human therapeutic evidence. Exercise-associated measurements and compounding discussions do not fill that gap.

sections.title: Original metabolic experiments
sections.body: The discovery study reported prevention of age-related and diet-induced insulin resistance in mice, alongside cellular metabolic work. That supports the proposed signaling role without establishing a human obesity or diabetes treatment.

sections.title: Human observation versus mouse intervention
sections.body: A later study administered MOTS-c to mice and assessed physical performance. Its human component measured endogenous peptide changes after exercise. The human observation cannot be presented as evidence that MOTS-c injections improve exercise capacity in people.

sections.title: What FDA’s 2026 review identified
sections.body: The review found no adequate human administration data to characterize safety and highlighted missing pharmacokinetic and toxicology information. Rapid degradation in experimental human blood raised an additional exposure question. Unknown safety cannot be summarized as an absence of side effects.

sections.title: Compounding and approval are separate
sections.body: MOTS-c was discussed in the 2026 compounding advisory process. That process does not establish FDA approval of a medicine, an effective indication or a validated long-term regimen.

sections.title: Is this an exercise replacement?
sections.body: The evidence does not show that administering MOTS-c reproduces the broad effects of human physical activity. A pathway shared with exercise is a research lead, not proof that one peptide can replace training, nutrition or management of diagnosed metabolic disease.

sections.title: Common questions
sections.body:
Does exercise research prove that injecting MOTS-c improves human fitness? No. The cited work includes measurements of natural peptide responses in humans and administration experiments in mice; these are different types of evidence.

Does naturally occurring mean a marketed injectable is safe? No. Exogenous exposure, product identity, impurities, degradation and immune responses require direct assessment, and FDA identified substantial gaps in human safety information.

name: Humanin
summary: Humanin is a mitochondrial-derived peptide investigated in cell survival, insulin action and aging biology. Animal experiments and human biomarker associations are intriguing, but there is no established human therapeutic role for injected humanin or proof that it extends human lifespan.
description: Humanin belongs to a family of short peptides associated with mitochondrial genetic sequences. Research includes native humanin and engineered analogs such as HNG, which can differ substantially in potency and exposure. Studies report protection from experimental cellular stress, altered insulin action in rodents and associations between circulating levels and age-related characteristics in people. These lines of evidence should remain separate. An association with healthy aging does not demonstrate that giving the peptide causes healthy aging, and effects of an engineered analog do not automatically define the benefit or risk of native humanin sold commercially.
mechanism: Humanin research involves several cell-survival and metabolic pathways rather than one fully validated clinical target. In an insulin-clamp study, central administration influenced peripheral insulin action through hypothalamic STAT3 signaling, while a potent analog produced related effects after peripheral administration in rodents. Such mechanistic experiments can establish pathway involvement in that model, but do not provide human exposure, delivery or long-term safety requirements.
keyTakeaway: Humanin is a research signal with promising mechanistic observations, not a validated anti-aging intervention. Native peptide, engineered analogs, animal treatment and human biomarker associations should not be collapsed into one efficacy claim.

sections.title: Insulin-action experiments
sections.body: An original study found improved insulin action with central humanin exposure and peripheral administration of potent derivatives in rodents. It implicated hypothalamic STAT3 signaling. These experiments do not establish an approved diabetes treatment or a comparable effect from routine human injection.

sections.title: What longevity research actually measured
sections.body: A later study reported lifespan effects in worms, metabolic and inflammatory effects in mice, and higher circulating levels in children of centenarians than comparison participants. Those are different experimental and observational findings, not a human lifespan-extension trial.

sections.title: Why HNG is not simply another label
sections.body: HNG is an engineered humanin analog used in some experiments. A change in sequence can alter potency, receptor interactions and exposure. A product described only as humanin should not inherit every result obtained with a modified analog.

sections.title: Unresolved human safety
sections.body: The cited studies do not establish clinical adverse-event rates, reproductive safety, interactions or consequences of prolonged human administration. Cell-survival activity itself is not a sufficient safety argument because biological effects depend on tissue, disease and exposure.

sections.title: Do higher natural levels prove supplementation works?
sections.body: No. A biomarker can reflect health, compensation or other confounding factors. Establishing a treatment requires controlled administration studies with clinically relevant outcomes, rather than assuming that reproducing an associated laboratory value will reproduce the associated health state.

sections.title: Common questions
sections.body:
Do higher humanin levels in some long-lived groups prove that supplementation extends life? No. An association can reflect other biological differences and cannot establish a treatment effect.

Is HNG identical to native humanin? No. HNG is a modified analog used in some experiments. Its results should retain that identity instead of being attributed automatically to an unmodified humanin product.
